searchText: lol, we gonna have the splurge 😀 credit to : <@!273808422753796097> Hey <@420951281910284289> totally hear what you’re saying and honestly we all really appreciate the crazy work the core devs have done on this. It’s very cool, coming from a tradfi / web2 background myself. I just wonder if the answer here is simply better documentation on either the EF site or ethereum.org I plan on attending the community call that Joshua and some of the other folks on ethereum.org are hosting next week but a simple, easy to find map or “org chart” of the structure of the broader ethereum community would be incredibly helpful for newcomers. Right now it’s a bit of a fragmented series of URLs, repos, and many disparate discord servers / telegrams. We don’t have to make the understanding of the humanistic side of ethereum cryptographic, if you know what I mean. Am coming at this from a place of wanting to help grow this ecosystem Yes I saw that. The product roadmap is very helpful. Someone should do exactly this for how the people and the teams are organized I’ll probably do something like this. It’s like an anthropomorphic study of ethereum. But present it in such a way that it is usable for non-crypto natives & folks like me who are only a few months into studying this <@552133098075193354> your pod with the Bankless guys was a great first step. I’ll try to reach out to them and see if we can collab on something that’s additive TIL Ethereum has 100 reorgs per day that is wasted bandwidth and io 🤔 ommers i have a security question about data sharding https://docs.ethhub.io/ethereum-roadmap/ethereum-2.0/stateless-clients/ so in my understanding of stateless clients, not every client needs to store the entire state of the blockchain and new nodes can enter the network and start "absorbing" new transactions since the chain will be sharded into 64 chains, doesn't this mean that a smaller number of nodes will now hold a smaller part of the blockchain, therefore making it easier to attack a group of nodes and modify their data? i think those are different than a reorg about 600 uncles/ommers per day and 100 reorgs oh wait as in blocks that don't even get included as ommers? ye. im guestimating that it increases Bandwidth and IO use by about 1% for each node 😛 likely going away after the merge tho due to more consistent block times. but lets see I'm assuming that as well Mostly will probably go away with PoS. One "risk" I'll point out if you work on this is that it will rapidly go out of date! I'd recommend trying to collaborate with an existing "information hub" (e.g. ethhub.io or ethereum.org) and add the knowledge there so you don't have the full burden of keeping it up to date forever 🙂 Thank god I can rely on the ethereum community to help with that! But I’m gonna try to get it started with ethereum.org <a:partywizard:884577076567502880> Also someone over on the Cosmos protocol (similar-ish vibe and openness as ethereum tbh + is a highly modular blockchain which is why I love both communities haha) came up with this super cool map of their “zones.” Not quite an “org chart” but is a related effort I think to help newcomers understand and appreciate the sheer diversity and size of this ecosystem. Ethereum is much more than just mainnet — didn’t appreciate that until I dove in https://mapofzones.com/ Appreciate the thoughtful response <@552133098075193354>! Im sure other pods like Unchained etc would love to host you if you have time. It’s helpful I think for non-core devs or other ethereum stakeholders to hear more directly from the people who help make this all possible. There’s so many people out there who want to help and pitch in — they just have a hard time figuring out the perfect entry point. So maybe we may need multiple entry points? Idk I’ll try to raise this issue on the community call with <@643099918998831144> Good thing Cami Russo is gonna turn this entire discord history into a move tho 😆<a:cketh:595706272658227251> That job for keeping records on the ecosystem sounds like being the “village elder” lmao 😂 Will eclipse attacks become easier after the merge since for example things like Infura cant just peer directly with mining pool anymore? there will be much more variance in the p2p network and which ip's valid blocks come from it seems so you will have to trust complete strangers on the p2p network more but i could be wrong I guess the question is how does Infura protect against eclipse attacks today, im guessing they have a few solid peers and direct connection with the known honest mining pools. But this will not be possible after the merge since blocks are going to be coming from all kinds of directions now. But i could be wrong Infura doesn’t peer directly with anyone today as far as I’m aware and doing so would increase their chances of being eclipsed because they’d be trusting those connections. The way to avoid eclipse attacks is to ensure you have a broad variety of peers. Basically eclipse attacks are a form of censorship and the answer is decentralisation.
